=== OPEN ISSUE A — entity classification (filter vs project) ===
Verified on prod: describeEntity(product=tm, entity="project") lists `list_entity_filter_details` in its `capabilities` array alongside get_project_by_integer_id, get_project_settings, list_projects, etc. — confirmed FILED UNDER entity=project.
describeEntity(product=tm, entity="filter") lists exactly 5 capabilities in its `capabilities` array: create_filter, delete_filter, get_filter, list_filters, update_filter. list_entity_filter_details is NOT among them.
searchCapability(product=tm, entity="filter", query="filter") returned total_matched=5, and those 5 results were exactly the same filter CRUD set (create_filter, get_filter, update_filter, list_filters, delete_filter) — list_entity_filter_details did not appear.
CONCLUSION: this reproduces on prod exactly as on preprod, and is expected to — it is a registry/index property (entity classification), not a live-API behavior, so it cannot differ by environment. list_entity_filter_details is UNREACHABLE via an entity=filter-scoped search on prod, and IS filed under entity=project, despite its own intent text describing it as pure filter-id hydration ("turn priority/status/case-type/custom-field ids, folder ids and user ids into names, colours and folder paths so a saved filter can be rendered"). This is a registry misclassification, confirmed identical on both environments.

=== OPEN ISSUE B — entity enum blocks test-plans: client-side vs server 4xx ===
Called invokeCapability(name=list_entity_filter_details, product=tm, path_params={project_id:332537, entity:"test-plans"}, query={"q[status]":"9319"}).
EXACT RESULT: `{"ok":false,"error":"'entity' must be one of: test-cases, trtc, test-runs"}` — no `http_response` key at all, no HTTP status code, no server-shaped error envelope (the capability's own declared error envelopes are `{success:false,error:{code,message,details}}`; this response has neither `success` nor that structure).
CONCLUSION: this is a CLIENT-SIDE rejection produced by the invokeCapability tool's own JSON-schema validation of the `entity` path_param enum — it never reaches the API server. This is distinct from, and happens BEFORE, the handler-level 400 that the preprod finding described (the handler itself also rejects entity=test-plans with a genuine 400, per describeCapability's own guidance: "'test-plans' passes the route constraint but is not in the handler's map and returns 400 — the route and the handler disagree"). On prod, that server-side 400 is UNREACHABLE through this MCP surface because the client-side enum check fires first and short-circuits the call — the same double-block (schema-level AND handler-level) confirmed on preprod is confirmed here too, with the schema-level block being the one that actually fires when going through invokeCapability.
